field.label: Field
field.says: The values of one field — of this entry or of the entries coming in from the left.

statementThesis.label: Thesis
statementThesis.says: The first sentence of block content — the thesis (of this entry or of the entries coming in from the left; any kind with a “Block content” field).

statementPart.label: Content part
statementPart.says: Block number n (1, 2, …) of block content: a paragraph as text, a list — each point separately, a table — each row (“Lk 1:35 — Acts 1:8”). Empty: all paragraphs.

statementTable.label: Table from content
statementTable.says: Table rows from block content as two sides: column A on the left, column B on the right (the same positions form a pair) — for “match pairs” or questions about a column.

statementSubjects.label: What it is about
statementSubjects.says: The entries the statement's reference fields point to (e.g. “About”) — with the place (e.g. “Lk 1:35”).

media.label: Image or sound
media.says: A file from a field — as a question: show the image, play the recording.

follow.label: Through references
follow.says: Follows references step by step (e.g. author, then their birthplace) and gives the entries at the end of the path.

list.label: List
list.says: A fixed list typed in by the author — e.g. extra correct answers or your own distractors.

entity.label: This entry
entity.says: The entry the card is made for — with its label.

filter.label: Filter
filter.says: Splits entries by a field: those whose field has a value from “Compare with” (or typed in), and the others — e.g. words in this card's language and words in other languages. Without a field it compares the entries themselves.

unique.label: No repeats
unique.says: Each entry (or text) only once — e.g. the languages of all words of a translation, each one once.

entries.label: Entries of a kind
entries.says: Entries of the chosen kind — all of them, or those whose field has a value from “Where field has” (or typed in): words with the same spelling, translations with this word, words in a given language. Can skip this entry and take a few at random.

pattern.label: Text pattern
pattern.says: Builds a text from the inputs: “Who wrote {0}?”. Several values on one input are joined with a comma.

mask.label: Mask
mask.says: Hides part of a text: the end, the beginning or random words. Gives the text with a gap, the hidden part and the whole.

fragments.label: Quote fragments
fragments.says: Splits a quote into pieces (7–13 characters) and arranges them in a tree: first the pieces, then what they make together. Connect “For each value”.

pick.label: Pick one
pick.says: Takes one value from a list (random, first or last) and gives it and the rest separately.

distractors.label: Distractors
distractors.says: Wrong answers to choose from: the same field of other entries of this kind, only from the current set, the author's list, or the values closest to the correct one.

each.label: For each value
each.says: Makes a separate card for each value from the left — each translation, each fragment of a quote.

pairs.label: Pairs
pairs.says: A pair from each entry: the field values matching the left side and those matching the right (without a right side: all the others) — e.g. from each translation the English and the Polish word. An entry without one of the sides is dropped.

pairsFields.label: Pairs from two fields
pairsFields.says: A pair from each entry: the field on the left (e.g. a text fragment) and the field on the right (empty: the entry's thesis) — for “match pairs”, e.g. five fragments of one work and their five theses. An entry without one of the sides is dropped.

random.label: Random value
random.says: Draws a number from a range (with a step) or one item from a list (typed here or coming from the left) — one template gives a different question every time (a “random” card: its history does not start over with each draw). “How many” > 1: that many different ones (no repeats) — e.g. 4 entries to put in order.

math.label: Operation
math.says: Calculates: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, power, logarithm, rounding, remainder.

calc.label: Calculate
calc.says: Calculates expressions in the drawing language — e.g. p0 * p1, mod(p0, 7), round(p0 / 3, 2), sqrt(p0), fmt(p0, 2) — each on its own line or after “;”, each gives one value (e.g. distractors “p0 + 1; p0 - 1; p0 * 2” for “Answer: single choice”). p0, p1, … are the first number of an input, n0, n1, … — how many values came, l0, l1, … — all values of the input as a list (entries as entries: sum(l0, it.masa), map(l0, it.label)). A result that is a list gives several values; a result that is not a number (division by zero) is dropped; when an input an expression uses gave no number, or no expression gave anything — the step fails and no card is made from this entry.

generate.label: Generator
generate.says: Draws a task: numbers from ranges ("params": [{"name": "s", "random": [20, 500], "step": 10}]), items from lists ({"name": "f", "values": ["sin", "cos"]}), entries from the base ({"name": "kation", "entry": {"kind": "@chem/jon", "where": "it.ladunek > 0"}}, several different ones: "entries" with "count"), calculates values ("let": [{"name": "v", "value": "s / t"}]) and checks conditions ("require": ["isint(v)"] — draws again, at most 60 times); "texts": [{"name": "pytanie", "value": "What is {a} + {b}?"}] — texts with values. In expressions "this" is this card's entry (this.pole); "only": "this.ladunek > 0" — only such entries of the kind get a card (others without a warning). Each name has its own output. When the task cannot be drawn, no card is made from this entry — with the reason in the preview.

aggregate.label: Aggregate
aggregate.says: Combines many values into one: sum, how many there are, smallest, largest, average — e.g. the sum of protons of a compound's components (a number field read through a reference to many entries: the same component twice counts twice). “Count” counts every value, also non-numeric ones (0 when nothing came); the others only numbers — without any number they give nothing, and no card is made from this entry.

compare.label: Comparison
compare.says: True or false from comparing two numbers or dates: “born before …?”.

when.label: Condition
when.says: The card is made only when the condition holds — e.g. when the field is filled in.

python.label: Python
python.says: Calculates in Python, in the browser (Pyodide): the function run(*inputs) returns a value or a list of values.

prompt.label: Question
prompt.says: What the learner sees: texts, images, recordings — in the order of the connections from top to bottom.

answerText.label: Answer: text
answerText.says: The learner types a text. The first value is the model answer; the next ones and “other correct” count too.

answerGap.label: Answer: gap in a quote
answerGap.says: The learner fills in a gap. Takes the text with a gap and the hidden part (from a mask) or a quote fragment.

answerNumber.label: Answer: number
answerNumber.says: The learner types a number; tolerance absolute or in percent, a unit to type beside it; with a quantity (e.g. torque) the answer's unit counts: another unit of the same quantity is converted, a unit of another quantity is an error.

answerDate.label: Answer: date
answerDate.says: The learner types a date with the required precision (year, month, day); tolerance in these units.

answerOne.label: Answer: single choice
answerOne.says: The learner picks one answer from the correct one and the distractors, in random order.

answerMany.label: Answer: multiple choice
answerMany.says: The learner marks all correct ones among the correct ones and the distractors.

answerTruefalse.label: Answer: true or false
answerTruefalse.says: The learner says “true” or “false”; the value comes e.g. from a comparison.

answerOrder.label: Answer: order
answerOrder.says: The learner puts the items in order — the order in which they come in.

answerMatch.label: Answer: match pairs
answerMatch.says: The learner joins pairs: items on the left with items on the right (the same positions on the lists form a pair).

answerFlash.label: Answer: flashcard
answerFlash.says: The learner turns the card over and rates themselves: knew it, partly, didn't know.

answerCode.label: Answer: code (Python)
answerCode.says: The learner writes a function in Python; Pyodide checks it in the browser on random cases.

answerPoint.label: Answer: point
answerPoint.says: The learner points to a place on a map (from a “place” field) or a point on an image.

card.label: Card
card.says: Assembles a card: question, answer and (after answering) an explanation from the connected entries. For generator tasks: “Hints” (texts, from gentle to specific) and “Solution” (a text with the drawn values and intermediate results — after answering).

error.filterNothing: The filter has nothing to compare with: connect “Compare with” or type a value.
error.entriesNothing: “Entries of a kind” with a field have nothing to compare with: connect “Where field has” or type a value.
error.pairsFields: Pairs need a field with the values (e.g. words) and a field to split them by (e.g. language).
error.pairsLeft: Pairs don't know what goes on the left: connect “Left: compare with” or type a value.
error.randomItems: “Random value”: {count} different items needed, there are {have}.
error.randomRange: “Random value”: the range has only {have} numbers, but {count} different ones are needed.
error.cannotCompute: This cannot be calculated (no number or division by zero).
error.calcEmpty: “Calculate” has no expression — type e.g. p0 + 1.
error.noExprNumber: No expression gave a number (e.g. division by zero).
error.generatorEmpty: The generator has nothing to draw — add "params", "let" or "texts".
error.noTask: The task could not be drawn.
error.compareNeeds: A comparison needs two numbers or dates.
